claim: IAV infection of mice generates CD69+CD103+ memory CD8+ T cell populations in lung-draining mediastinal lymph nodes (mLNs).
source: We show that IAV infection of mice generates CD69+CD103+and other memory CD8+T cell populations in lung-draining mediastinal lymph nodes (mLNs) from circulating naive or memory CD8+T cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing CD69+CD103+ populations in mLN after IAV infection.

claim: Repeated antigen exposure generates quaternary memory (4M) CD8+ T cells that protect mLN from viral infection better than 1M CD8+ T cells.
source: Repeated antigen exposure, mimicking seasonal IAV infections, generates quaternary memory (4M) CD8+T cells that protect mLN from viral infection better than 1M CD8+T cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing enhanced viral control in mLN by 4M compared to 1M CD8+ T cells.

claim: Better protection by 4M CD8+ T cells associates with enhanced granzyme A/B expression.
source: Better protection by 4M CD8+T cells associates with enhanced granzyme A/B expression and stable maintenance of mLN CD69+CD103+4M CD8+T cells, vs the steady decline of CD69+CD103+1M CD8+T cells
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing increased granzyme A/B expression in 4M cells and correlation with protection.

claim: 4M CD69+CD103+ CD8+ T cells are stably maintained in mLN while 1M CD69+CD103+ CD8+ T cells steadily decline.
source: Better protection by 4M CD8+T cells associates with enhanced granzyme A/B expression and stable maintenance of mLN CD69+CD103+4M CD8+T cells, vs the steady decline of CD69+CD103+1M CD8+T cells
evidence: This claim is supported by longitudinal experimental data showing differential maintenance of 1M vs 4M Trm populations.

claim: The durability of protective CD69+CD103+ 4M vs 1M in the mLN parallels the durability in the lung after IAV infection.
source: Better protection by 4M CD8+T cells associates with enhanced granzyme A/B expression and stable maintenance of mLN CD69+CD103+4M CD8+T cells, vs the steady decline of CD69+CD103+1M CD8+T cells, paralleling the durability of protective CD69+CD103+4M vs 1M in the lung after IAV infection.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of data from mLN and lung Trm populations and references to prior work.

claim: Coordinated upregulation in canonical Trm-associated genes occurs in circulating 4M vs 1M populations.
source: Coordinated upregulation in canonical Trm-associated genes occurs in circulating 4M vs 1M populations without the enrichment of canonical downregulated Trm genes.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data showing differential gene expression between 1M and 4M circulating populations.

claim: Circulating 4M populations do not show enrichment of canonical downregulated Trm genes.
source: Coordinated upregulation in canonical Trm-associated genes occurs in circulating 4M vs 1M populations without the enrichment of canonical downregulated Trm genes.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and GSEA analysis showing lack of enrichment of downregulated Trm genes.

claim: Repeated antigen exposure arms circulating memory CD8+ T cells with enhanced capacity to form long-lived populations of Trm.
source: Thus, repeated antigen exposure arms circulating memory CD8+T cells with enhanced capacity to form long-lived populations of Trm that enhance control of viral infections of the mLN.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing enhanced Trm formation and durability from 4M circulating precursors.

claim: Repeated antigen exposure enhances control of viral infections of the mLN.
source: Thus, repeated antigen exposure arms circulating memory CD8+T cells with enhanced capacity to form long-lived populations of Trm that enhance control of viral infections of the mLN.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing enhanced viral control in mLN by 4M cells.

claim: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a global health burden despite long-term worldwide efforts into vaccine development.
source: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a global heath burden despite long-term worldwide efforts into vaccine development (Paget et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature on IAV disease burden.

claim: Current gold-standard vaccinations primarily induce strong and durable antibody responses directed toward the HA and NA proteins of IAV.
source: Current gold-standard vaccinations primarily induce strong and durable antibody responses directed toward the HA and NA proteins of IAV (Padilla-Quirarte et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published literature on IAV vaccines.

claim: Viral antigenic shift and drift cause targets of protective antibody responses to be under selective immune pressure and exhibit high mutation rates.
source: However, due to viral antigenic shift and drift, the targets of protective antibody responses are under selective immune pressure and exhibit high mutation rates, reducing the effectiveness of seasonal vaccine approaches (Thyagarajan and Bloom, 2014; Visher et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on viral evolution.

claim: Antigenic shift and drift reduce the effectiveness of seasonal vaccine approaches.
source: However, due to viral antigenic shift and drift, the targets of protective antibody responses are under selective immune pressure and exhibit high mutation rates, reducing the effectiveness of seasonal vaccine approaches (Thyagarajan and Bloom, 2014; Visher et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and represents established knowledge.

claim: Some level of protective immunity can be acquired in humans against distinct heterosubtypic influenza infections.
source: Recent reports demonstrate that some level of protective immunity can be acquired in humans against distinct heterosubtypic influenza infections (McMichael et al., 1983; Sridhar et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published human studies.

claim: Protection against heterosubtypic influenza infections can be mediated by memory CD8+ T cells targeting conserved antigens such as the IAV nucleoprotein (NP).
source: and animal studies show that this protection can be mediated by memory CD8+ T cells targeting conserved antigens such as the IAV nucleoprotein (NP; Yewdell et al., 1985; Slütter et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published animal studies.

claim: A local population of tissue-resident memory CD8+ T cells within the lung parenchyma (lung Trm cells) is associated with acquired protection following natural or live-attenuated influenza infections.
source: Recent evidence suggests a local population of tissue-resident memory CD8+ T cells within the lung parenchyma (lung Trm cells) is associated with this acquired protection following natural or live-attenuated influenza infections (Wu et al., 2014; Van Braeckel-Budimir et al., 2018; Slütter et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies on lung Trm cells.

claim: Trm cell numbers wane within the lung.
source: Unfortunately, and in contrast to the long-lived nature of Trm cells in numerous peripheral and mucosal tissues, Trm cell numbers wane within the lung
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies showing decline of lung Trm.

claim: Loss of lung Trm cells strongly correlates with the loss of protective immunity to subsequent heterosubtypic IAV infections.
source: and their loss strongly correlates with the loss of protective immunity to subsequent heterosubtypic IAV infections (Wu et al., 2014; Van Braeckel-Budimir et al., 2018; Slütter et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies showing correlation between Trm decline and loss of protection.

claim: The majority of current murine experimental systems rely on one or two sequential IAV infections.
source: Despite the annual IAV exposures in humans, the majority of current murine experimental systems rely on one or two sequential IAV infections.
evidence: This claim represents a statement about the state of the field based on knowledge of published literature.

claim: The inability to carry out multiple IAV infections of the same mouse is due to the generation of cross-reactive antibodies and the dearth of mouse-adapted influenza strains.
source: In part, this is due to the inability to carry out multiple IAV infections of the same mouse due to the generation of cross-reactive antibodies and the dearth of mouse-adapted influenza strains (Van Braeckel-Budimir et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published work explaining technical limitations.

claim: A system was devised where influenza-specific naive or circulating splenic memory CD8+ T cells with a defined number of antigen exposures are isolated and passaged to naive hosts that receive a subsequent intranasal IAV infection.
source: To address the impact of repetitive IAV infections on lung Trm, we devised a system where influenza-specific naive or circulating splenic memory CD8+ T cells with a defined number of antigen exposures are isolated and passaged to naive hosts that receive a subsequent intranasal IAV infection (Van Braeckel-Budimir et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental system used in the study, supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The adoptive transfer system generates both lung Trm cells and circulating memory CD8+ T cells that have selectively undergone a defined number of antigenic encounters after lung IAV infection.
source: This system generates both lung Trm cells and circulating memory CD8+ T cells that have selectively undergone a defined number of antigenic encounters after lung IAV infection and reflects the repetitive annual infectious nature of influenza within the human population.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental system and is supported by data from the study.

claim: The adoptive transfer system reflects the repetitive annual infectious nature of influenza within the human population.
source: This system generates both lung Trm cells and circulating memory CD8+ T cells that have selectively undergone a defined number of antigenic encounters after lung IAV infection and reflects the repetitive annual infectious nature of influenza within the human population.
evidence: This claim represents an interpretation of the experimental system's relevance to human biology.

claim: Repeated IAV exposures substantially enhanced the durability of lung CD69+CD103+ CD8+ T cells.
source: Utilizing this system, we described key enhancements in both the durability and protective capacity of lung Trm cells generated by repeated influenza antigen exposures (Van Braeckel-Budimir et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior published work from the authors.

claim: Repeated IAV exposures prolonged heterosubtypic immunity.
source: However, repeated IAV exposures substantially enhanced the durability of 4M lung CD69+ CD103+ CD8+ T cells and prolonged heterosubtypic immunity (Van Braeckel-Budimir et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior published work from the authors.

claim: Populations phenotypically resembling Trm cells are found within the lymph nodes of both humans and mice.
source: Recent evidence suggests that in addition to non-lymphoid tissues, populations phenotypically resembling Trm cells are also found within the lymph nodes of both humans and mice
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Lymph node Trm-like populations maintain residence during parabiosis experiments.
source: and interestingly, these populations maintain residence during parabiosis experiments (Schenkel et al., 2014a; Beura et al., 2018; Kumar et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published parabiosis studies.

claim: Lymph node Trm cells can be generated in tissue dLN after local infection.
source: These cells can be generated in tissue dLN after local infection or derive from pre-existing tissue Trm cells (Beura et al., 2018; Park et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Lymph node Trm cells can derive from pre-existing tissue Trm cells.
source: These cells can be generated in tissue dLN after local infection or derive from pre-existing tissue Trm cells (Beura et al., 2018; Park et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Trm cells in non-lymphoid tissues predominantly act as sentinels, able to quickly activate and produce IFNγ upon the recognition of cognate antigen.
source: Trm cells in non-lymphoid tissues predominantly act as sentinels, able to quickly activate and produce IFNγ upon the recognition of cognate antigen, which simultaneously induces the recruitment of circulating immune cells and activates local innate immunity that further propagates the inflammatory signal (Schenkel et al., 2014b; Schenkel et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies on Trm function.

claim: Trm cell activation induces the recruitment of circulating immune cells and activates local innate immunity.
source: Trm cells in non-lymphoid tissues predominantly act as sentinels, able to quickly activate and produce IFNγ upon the recognition of cognate antigen, which simultaneously induces the recruitment of circulating immune cells and activates local innate immunity that further propagates the inflammatory signal (Schenkel et al., 2014b; Schenkel et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies on Trm function.

claim: Selective non-lymphoid Trm populations have direct cytotoxic capabilities.
source: Alternatively, selective non-lymphoid Trm populations are described to have direct cytotoxic capabilities (Cheuk et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published work.

claim: It remains unknown if LN Trm cells possess similar properties to those described for non-lymphoid Trm populations.
source: However, it remains unknown if LN Trm cells possess similar properties to those described for non-lymphoid Trm populations and whether LN Trm can mediate protective immunity.
evidence: This claim represents a knowledge gap identified by the authors.

claim: It remains unknown whether LN Trm can mediate protective immunity.
source: However, it remains unknown if LN Trm cells possess similar properties to those described for non-lymphoid Trm populations and whether LN Trm can mediate protective immunity.
evidence: This claim represents a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Primary IAV infection generates Trm cells within the lung-draining mLN.
source: Consistent with a recent study, we show that primary IAV infection generates Trm cells within the lung-draining mLN and that these cells mirror the cell surface marker expression and residence of Trm cells within the lung (Suarez-Ramirez et al., 2019; Stolley et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in the manuscript and citations to recent studies.

claim: mLN Trm cells mirror the cell surface marker expression and residence of Trm cells within the lung.
source: Consistent with a recent study, we show that primary IAV infection generates Trm cells within the lung-draining mLN and that these cells mirror the cell surface marker expression and residence of Trm cells within the lung (Suarez-Ramirez et al., 2019; Stolley et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by data comparing mLN and lung Trm phenotypes.

claim: Repeated IAV encounters impart numerous changes in the transcriptional and functional landscape of LN Trm cell populations.
source: Importantly, we find that repeated IAV encounters impart numerous changes in the transcriptional and functional landscape of LN Trm cell populations, including enhanced ability to defend the lymph node against viral infection.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq and functional data in the manuscript.

claim: Repeated IAV encounters enhance the ability of LN Trm cells to defend the lymph node against viral infection.
source: Importantly, we find that repeated IAV encounters impart numerous changes in the transcriptional and functional landscape of LN Trm cell populations, including enhanced ability to defend the lymph node against viral infection.
evidence: This claim is supported by viral challenge data showing enhanced protection by 4M cells.

claim: Multiple antigen encounters poise circulating memory CD8+ T cell populations for rapid conversion to durable Trm cells in response to tissue infections.
source: These data suggest that multiple antigen encounters poise circulating memory CD8+ T cell populations for rapid conversion to durable Trm cells in response to tissue infections, a concept with direct relevance toward effective vaccine design.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data showing Trm gene expression in circulating 4M cells and durability data.

claim: The concept that multiple antigen encounters poise circulating memory CD8+ T cells for Trm conversion has direct relevance toward effective vaccine design.
source: These data suggest that multiple antigen encounters poise circulating memory CD8+ T cell populations for rapid conversion to durable Trm cells in response to tissue infections, a concept with direct relevance toward effective vaccine design.
evidence: This claim represents speculation about the translational implications of the findings.

claim: IAV infection of naive C57BL6 mice generates endogenous NP366 MHC class I tetramer+ cells in the mLN and non-draining cervical lymph nodes (cLNs) 90 days post-infection.
source: To address the generality of this observation, we infected naive C57BL6 (B6) mice IN with the IAV X31 (H3N2) and analyzed endogenous NP366 MHC class I tetramer+ cells in the mLN and non-draining cervical lymph nodes (cLNs) 90 days later (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: CD69+ CD103- NP366 tetramer+ cells are observed in both mLN and cLN after systemic LCMV infection.
source: As previously described after systemic LCMV infection (Beura et al., 2018), CD69+ CD103- NP366 tetramer+ cells were observed in both mLN and cLN (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 1B and citation to prior work.

claim: CD69+ CD103+ NP366 tetramer+ cells are primarily localized within the mLN after IAV infection.
source: Consistent with the prior report with TCR-Tg T cells, we also observed an additional population of CD69+ CD103+ NP366 tetramer+ cells primarily localized within the mLN (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 1B showing differential localization.

claim: IAV infection generates CD69+ CD103- and CD69+ CD103+ mLN T cells from the endogenous repertoire.
source: Thus, IAV infection generates CD69+ CD103- and CD69+ CD103+ mLN T cells from the endogenous repertoire.
evidence: This claim is supported by data using endogenous tetramer+ cells rather than TCR-Tg cells.

claim: Both IN infections with IAV PR8-GP33 and VacV-GP33 generated CD69+ CD103 and CD69+ CD103+ P14 cells within the mLN at 30 days post-infection.
source: Both IN infections generated CD69+ CD103 and CD69+ CD103+ P14 s within the mLN at 30 days post-infection; however, the frequency of CD69+ CD103+ P14 cells was lower in Vac-GP33 infected mice (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The frequency of CD69+ CD103+ P14 cells was lower in Vac-GP33 infected mice compared to PR8-GP33 infected mice.
source: Both IN infections generated CD69+ CD103 and CD69+ CD103+ P14 s within the mLN at 30 days post-infection; however, the frequency of CD69+ CD103+ P14 cells was lower in Vac-GP33 infected mice (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative data in Figure 1D.

claim: CD69+ CD103+ Trm were not generated in the mLN or iLN after systemic LCMV infection.
source: In contrast, CD69+ CD103+ Trm were not generated in the mLN or iLN after systemic LCMV infection, although we did find the previously described (Stolley et al., 2020) CD69+ CD103 P14 in these SLO (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: CD69+ CD103 P14 cells are found in mLN and iLN after systemic LCMV infection.
source: In contrast, CD69+ CD103+ Trm were not generated in the mLN or iLN after systemic LCMV infection, although we did find the previously described (Stolley et al., 2020) CD69+ CD103 P14 in these SLO (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 1F and citation to prior work.

claim: CD69+ CD103+ mLN Trm are not uniformly generated in response to infection.
source: Thus, CD69+ CD103+ mLN Trm are not uniformly generated in response to infection, suggesting that the respiratory route of infection may be critical for these populations.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential generation of CD69+CD103+ cells after respiratory vs systemic infection.

claim: The respiratory route of infection may be critical for generation of CD69+ CD103+ mLN Trm populations.
source: Thus, CD69+ CD103+ mLN Trm are not uniformly generated in response to infection, suggesting that the respiratory route of infection may be critical for these populations.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the observed differences between respiratory and systemic infections.

claim: Both endogenous and TCR-transgenic CD69+ CD103+ memory CD8+ T cells were generated specifically in the lung-draining mLN following two intranasal but not a systemic viral infection.
source: These data demonstrated that both endogenous and TCR-transgenic CD69+ CD103+ memory CD8+ T cells were generated specifically in the lung-draining mLN following two intranasal but not a systemic viral infection and that generation of these populations was not limited to IAV infection.
evidence: This claim summarizes data from multiple experiments with different infection models.

claim: Generation of CD69+ CD103+ mLN populations is not limited to IAV infection.
source: These data demonstrated that both endogenous and TCR-transgenic CD69+ CD103+ memory CD8+ T cells were generated specifically in the lung-draining mLN following two intranasal but not a systemic viral infection and that generation of these populations was not limited to IAV infection.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing CD69+CD103+ generation after VacV-GP33 infection.

claim: The local protective capacity of LN memory CD8+ T cells remains undefined.
source: It is notable that the local protective capacity of LN memory CD8+ T cells remains undefined, although these cells can be reactivated and migrate to the lung parenchyma after IAV challenge (Paik and Farber, 2021).
evidence: This claim identifies a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: LN memory CD8+ T cells can be reactivated and migrate to the lung parenchyma after IAV challenge.
source: It is notable that the local protective capacity of LN memory CD8+ T cells remains undefined, although these cells can be reactivated and migrate to the lung parenchyma after IAV challenge (Paik and Farber, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Direct rechallenge experiments by the same route of infection result in the pathogen initially encountering protective Trm in the primary infected tissue before reaching the dLN.
source: Interrogating this question is technically challenging, because direct rechallenge experiments by the same route of infection result in the pathogen initially encountering protective Trm in the primary infected tissue before reaching the dLN.
evidence: This claim explains a technical challenge in studying LN Trm protection.

claim: Virus can be detected in the mLN at 24 hr post-infection of naive hosts with IAV.
source: This issue is further complicated in the IAV model, although virus can be detected in the mLN at 24 hr post-infection of naive hosts (Flynn et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published work.

claim: IAV does not efficiently replicate in the mLN making assessment of virus clearance by memory CD8+ T cells problematic.
source: IAV does not efficiently replicate in this tissue making assessment of virus clearance by memory CD8+ T cells problematic.
evidence: This claim explains a technical limitation of using IAV to study mLN Trm protection.

claim: The recurring nature of IAV infections means that humans are likely to experience multiple infections causing their memory T cells to experience repetitive antigen encounters.
source: An additional issue is that the recurring nature of IAV infections means that humans are likely to experience multiple infections causing their memory T cells to experience repetitive antigen encounters, whereas mouse studies are generally restricted to one or two sequential IAV infections.
evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about human IAV exposure patterns.

claim: Mouse studies are generally restricted to one or two sequential IAV infections.
source: An additional issue is that the recurring nature of IAV infections means that humans are likely to experience multiple infections causing their memory T cells to experience repetitive antigen encounters, whereas mouse studies are generally restricted to one or two sequential IAV infections.
evidence: This claim represents a statement about the state of experimental models.

claim: At 100 days post-infection, 1M and 4M mice had similar frequencies of circulating P14 cells in the blood.
source: At 100 days post-infection, 1M and 4M mice had similar frequencies of circulating P14 cells in the blood (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Total P14 were ~4× higher in the mLN of 4M vs 1M mice at 100 days post-infection.
source: Total P14 were ~4× higher in the mLN of 4M vs 1M mice (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: An ~50× increase in the number of CD69+ CD103+ mLN P14 was observed in 4M vs 1M mice at 100 days post-infection.
source: However, an ~50× increase in the number of CD69+ CD103+ mLN P14 was observed in 4M vs 1M mice at this time point (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: IP challenge with LCMV resulted in high mLN virus titers at 3 days post-infection in naive mice.
source: IP challenge with LCMV resulted in high mLN virus titers at 3 days post-infection in naive mice, whereas mice with 1M P14 trended toward reduced virus titers, although this was not statistically discernable.
evidence: This claim is supported by viral titer data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Mice with 1M P14 trended toward reduced virus titers in the mLN, although this was not statistically discernable.
source: IP challenge with LCMV resulted in high mLN virus titers at 3 days post-infection in naive mice, whereas mice with 1M P14 trended toward reduced virus titers, although this was not statistically discernable.
evidence: This claim is supported by viral titer data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Mice with 4M P14 exhibited robust control of LCMV in the mLN, with most mice exhibiting undetectable virus titers.
source: In contrast, mice with 4M P14 exhibited robust control of LCMV in the mLN, with most mice exhibiting undetectable virus titers (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by viral titer data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: 4M mice reduced virus titers in the spleen after LCMV challenge.
source: Of note, 4M mice also reduced virus titers in the spleen (Figure 2E) suggesting the possibility that control of LCMV in the LN may decrease virus spread within the host.
evidence: This claim is supported by viral titer data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Control of LCMV in the LN may decrease virus spread within the host.
source: Of note, 4M mice also reduced virus titers in the spleen (Figure 2E) suggesting the possibility that control of LCMV in the LN may decrease virus spread within the host.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the observation of reduced splenic titers.

claim: It is possible that the 4M cells in the spleen may have conferred enhanced immunity in this tissue.
source: However, it is also possible that the 4M cells in the spleen may have conferred enhanced immunity in this tissue.
evidence: This claim represents an alternative explanation for reduced splenic titers.

claim: FTY720 treatment discernably but modestly increased virus titers in the mLN of naive mice.
source: FTY720 treatment discernably but modestly increased virus titers in the mLN of naive mice (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by viral titer data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: FTY720 treatment did not influence virus control by 4M P14 in the mLN.
source: In contrast, FTY720 treatment did not influence virus control by 4M P14.
evidence: This claim is supported by viral titer data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Tissue-localized 4M CD8+ T cells have the capacity to control virus infection of the mLN without the aid of the circulating memory CD8+ T cell pool.
source: Together, these data show that tissue-localized 4M CD8+ T cells have the capacity to control virus infection of the mLN without the aid of the circulating memory CD8+ T cell pool.
evidence: This claim is supported by FTY720 treatment data showing protection without circulating cell recruitment.

claim: 1M lung CD69+ CD103+ CD8+ T cells wane with time after IAV infection resulting in a loss of heterosubtypic immunity.
source: Indeed, 1M lung CD69+ CD103+ CD8+ T cells wane with time after IAV infection resulting in a loss of heterosubtypic immunity (Wu et al., 2014; Slütter et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Repeated IAV exposures substantially enhanced the durability of 4M lung CD69+ CD103+ CD8+ T cells and prolonged heterosubtypic immunity.
source: However, repeated IAV exposures substantially enhanced the durability of 4M lung CD69+ CD103+ CD8+ T cells and prolonged heterosubtypic immunity (Van Braeckel-Budimir et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior published work from the authors.

claim: The total number of 4M P14 within the mLN exceeded the number of 1M at early memory time points.
source: The total number of 4M P14 within the mLN exceeded the number of 1M at early memory time points (Figure 3A)
evidence: This claim is supported by longitudinal data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Both 1M and 4M total P14 populations in mLN were similar in number from days 150 to 250 post-infection.
source: but both populations were similar in number from days 150 to 250 post-infection.
evidence: This claim is supported by longitudinal data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 1M CD69+ CD103+ mLN cells showed a steady decline in frequency from days 30 to 250 post-infection.
source: Within the CD69+ CD103+ compartment, 1M mLN cells showed a steady decline in frequency (Figure 3B) and total numbers (Figure 3C) from days 30 to 250 post-infection
evidence: This claim is supported by longitudinal data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: 1M CD69+ CD103+ mLN cells showed a steady decline in total numbers from days 30 to 250 post-infection.
source: Within the CD69+ CD103+ compartment, 1M mLN cells showed a steady decline in frequency (Figure 3B) and total numbers (Figure 3C) from days 30 to 250 post-infection
evidence: This claim is supported by longitudinal data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: 4M CD69+ CD103+ CD8+ T cells were largely maintained in frequency and total numbers from days 30 to 250 post-infection.
source: while 4M CD8+ T cells were largely maintained in frequency and total numbers over the same time frame.
evidence: This claim is supported by longitudinal data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: The observation of enhanced durability of 4M mLN Trm was similar to prior observations with lung Trm cells.
source: This observation was similar to our prior observations with lung Trm cells (Van Braeckel-Budimir et al., 2018; Slütter et al., 2017), suggesting similar extended survival properties of the lung and mLN 4M Trm cell populations derived from circulating 3M precursors.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison to prior published work.

claim: Lung and mLN 4M Trm cell populations derived from circulating 3M precursors have similar extended survival properties.
source: This observation was similar to our prior observations with lung Trm cells (Van Braeckel-Budimir et al., 2018; Slütter et al., 2017), suggesting similar extended survival properties of the lung and mLN 4M Trm cell populations derived from circulating 3M precursors.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the parallel durability patterns in lung and mLN.

claim: Total numbers of 1M P14s greatly exceeded those of 4M within the non-draining iLN at all time points.
source: In contrast, total numbers of 1M P14s greatly exceeded those of 4M within the non-draining iLN (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) at all time points.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CD103+ Trm cells were not observed in the non-draining iLN.
source: Similar to the endogenous population, CD103+ Trm cells were not observed in the non-draining iLN, with minimal frequencies of CD103+ Trm cells among either 1M or 4M populations (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: IAV-induced CD69+ CD103+ memory cells in the draining mLN wane with time.
source: Thus, analogous to lung parenchyma Trm cells, IAV-induced CD69+ CD103+ memory cells in the draining mLN wane with time, and repeated antigen exposures substantially extend the durability of this mLN memory CD8+ T cell population.
evidence: This claim is supported by longitudinal data showing decline of 1M Trm.

claim: Repeated antigen exposures substantially extend the durability of mLN CD69+ CD103+ memory CD8+ T cell populations.
source: Thus, analogous to lung parenchyma Trm cells, IAV-induced CD69+ CD103+ memory cells in the draining mLN wane with time, and repeated antigen exposures substantially extend the durability of this mLN memory CD8+ T cell population.
evidence: This claim is supported by longitudinal data showing maintenance of 4M Trm.

claim: The increased durability of CD69+ CD103+ 4M CD8+ T cells at day 100 post-infection likely played an important role in their enhanced ability to control local virus infection.
source: Importantly, the increased durability of CD69+ CD103+ 4M CD8+ T cells at day 100 post-infection likely played an important role in their enhanced ability to control local virus infection.
